name: Lucky
ambiguities: Lucky is a distinct observable label even though its legal move set is ordinary chess.

name: Eisoptrophobia
description: A piece cannot capture an opposing piece of the same type.
ambiguities: Promotion is classified by the pre-move pawn; en-passant captures a pawn.

name: Gloomstalker
description: Captures may only be made from dark squares.
ambiguities: Dark squares use standard chessboard coloring with a1 dark.

name: Noblesse Oblige
description: Kings and queens may capture only kings or queens.
ambiguities: Standard chess never represents king capture as an ordinary legal move.

name: Bongcloud
description: While the king is on its color-relative back rank, only pawns and kings may move.
ambiguities: Castling is a king move and remains permitted when standard-legal.

name: Eat Your Vegetables
description: Until the opponent has at most four pawns, only pawns may be captured.
ambiguities: The restriction lifts at four remaining opposing pawns, matching the wording 'only has 4'.

name: Horse Eats First
description: While the affected player has a knight, only knights may capture.
ambiguities: A promoted knight counts as a current knight.

name: Messy Divorce
description: Pieces cannot cross between queenside files a-d and kingside files e-h.
ambiguities: Queenside and kingside are interpreted as files a-d and e-h; kingside castling stays within e-h, while queenside castling crosses the boundary and is forbidden.

name: Body Snatcher
description: Lose when the opponent captures a non-pawn piece with an equivalent piece.
ambiguities: Piece equivalence uses current mover and captured types.

name: Castle Doctrine
description: Lose when the opponent captures a rook.
ambiguities: Promoted rooks count by current captured type.

name: My Kingdom for a Horse
description: Lose when the opponent captures a knight.
ambiguities: Promoted knights count by current captured type.

name: Octomom
description: Lose after the opponent captures eight pieces.
ambiguities: Every captured piece, including pawns, counts; standard chess never captures kings.

name: Pawn Battle
description: Lose when holding fewer pawns than the opponent.
ambiguities: Promoted pieces no longer count as pawns.

name: Edgelord
description: Lose when holding fewer pieces on the rim than the opponent.
ambiguities: The rim is the outside files a/h and ranks 1/8; all piece types count.

name: Botez Gambit
description: At the start of turn eleven, have no queen while the opponent has a queen.
ambiguities: Turn eleven is standard FEN fullmove 11 and is checked once for each color; promoted queens count.
